panels.title: People-search volume + zero-result rate
panels.description: WHAT: rate of people-search requests split by outcome (hit vs zero_result), plus the zero-result RATE (zero_result / total) as a search-quality signal. HOW: rate over stacks_search_people_count_total{outcome=…}, emitted once per GET /api/search/users in UserSearchController.index/2 with outcome=:zero_result when the result list is empty (never the query string — PII/cardinality). MEANS: mostly-hit with a small zero_result trickle is healthy discovery; the zero_result rate is how often readers search and find nobody. WATCH: a rising zero-result rate means search feels empty — retune the trigram/ILIKE matching or surface a 'no matches' UX; a total-volume spike with flat hits can indicate scraping or enumeration.

panels.title: Public-profile 404 rate
panels.description: WHAT: the fraction of public-profile resolutions that 404 (not_found / total), alongside the raw ok vs not_found rates. HOW: rate over stacks_profile_view_count_total{outcome=…}, emitted once per /u/:handle read in ProfileController.with_visible_profile/3 with outcome=:not_found on BOTH the absent-handle branch and the ghost/block 404 branch (never the handle — PII). MEANS: a low, steady not_found rate is normal (typos, stale links); the ratio is the broken-link / hidden-profile friction signal. WATCH: a sustained spike in the 404 rate means many hits on ghost/blocked/absent handles — broken external links or handle-enumeration probing; correlate with the profile/search rate-limit 429s.

panels.title: Public-shelf pagination-cap hits
panels.description: WHAT: rate of public shelf-browse responses that the public_shelf_cap (default 500) actually truncated. HOW: rate over stacks_shelf_browse_capped_count_total, emitted by ProfileController.render_shelf/4 ONLY when the visible-placement count exceeded the cap (never per placement). MEANS: normally near-zero — most shelves are well under 500 visible placements, so the cap rarely bites. WATCH: frequent cap hits mean someone is walking very large shelves (a genuine power-reader collection or a scraper paginating a public shelf); a sustained rise confirms the bound is doing its job and is worth correlating with the profile-404 and search-volume panels.

panels.title: Handle claims over time
panels.description: WHAT: rate of public /u/:handle claims — a profile update that set or changed the reader's handle. HOW: rate over stacks_handle_claimed_count_total, emitted by Stacks.Accounts.update_profile/2 only when the changeset actually changed:handle (never the handle value — untagged). MEANS: this is the adoption curve for public handles — a low, steady trickle as readers opt into a public /u/:handle presence, with occasional bumps when someone renames. WATCH: a sudden spike could be a rename campaign or automated account setup; a flatline at zero after launch means readers are not discovering or bothering with the handle-claim flow in Settings.
